a new program, SCLONE, has been developed which improves the quality of diffraction images that have no serial oscillation images by combining a least-squared procedure and the program MOSFLMs.

the scaling of a single image with a reference data-set significantly improves the quality of the structure amplitudes obtained from a crystal with a steep rocking curve, such as the present crystal.

the development of a method for processing one-shot images and with the application of the method to a crystal of the protein, the ribonuclease H from the human immunodeficiency virus (HIV).
the development of the SCLONE program for the processing of oscillation images that do not have serial oscillation images.
the scaling of one-shot oscillations images with the reference data set.

the SCLONE program is a useful tool for improving the quality of the diffraction images of crystals that have been processed by the program MOSFLMS.

the program SCLONE is useful for processing diffraction images that contain a few or no reflections, and it can be used to improve the quality of the reflection data from the initial processing with the program MOSFILM.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SCLONE is a very useful tool to improve the accuracy of the scaling of one-shot oscillations images.
the present method of scaling one-shot images by SCLONE is a useful tool for the analysis of the data set of a protein crystal.
the SCLONE calculation can be used to improve the quality of the reflection intensities of one-shot diffraction data sets, which have no serial oscillation images.

the present program SCLONE can be used to process one-shot oscillation diffraction images and to improve the quality of the reflection intensities.
the scaling procedure of SCLONE is effective to obtain accurate structure amplitudes for one-shot oscillation data.
the SCLONE program can be used to scale one-shot oscillation data, even when there is a large mosaic spread and/or the data are of low quality.
